incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated 5xx rate from infer-runtime clusters in us-west-2. Multiple segfaults observed; paging rotation triggered for oncall-sre. https://incidents.redwood/3632107777

maria (oncall-sre): acked. I'm pulling realtime metrics now — seeing a 12% 502/5xx spike across inference-prod-west-1 and west-2.

kevin (runtime-lead): on it. early signal shows segfaults in the quantized attention kernel after KV cache growth. stack traces pointing to native kernel.

jess (eng-oncall): tagging runtime team. any quick fallback we can flip to avoid customer impact?

kevin (runtime-lead): yes — start routing traffic away from the affected node pool to the standby pool and enable model-variant fallback to non-quantized v2 for critical customers. Steps:
- temporarily update routing rule: /route/infra -> pool-standby-west2
- set model_fallback_policy: prefer=redwood/open-v2-cpu, max_tokens=1024

maria (oncall-sre): executing reroute now. running:
```bash
kubectl --context=prod-west2 label nodes inference-pool-quant unstable=true && 
./routingctl set-backend --service infer-api --to standby-west2
```

maria (oncall-sre): reroute done. traffic shifted ~60% over 40s. 5xx rate dropped to 4% in west-2; still elevated in west-1.

kevin (runtime-lead): thanks. I'm collecting heap/kvcache growth samples. attaching a representative crash log snippet:
```text
PID 14237: signal 11 (SEGV), thread 0x1f4a
#0  0x7f9a3b2e in run_attention_quantized(void*) +0x3f
#1  0x7f9a3c10 in model_runner::exec +0x120
#2  0x55aa7f in inference_loop +0x2b
SEGV at 0x0 (read from NULL)
```

kevin (runtime-lead): root cause hypothesis: kvcache resizing path hits a race when using the quant kernel; on large prefix loads we occasionally deref NULL. patch ready to disable the problematic path and fallback to the safe attention implementation.

jess (eng-oncall): can we hotpatch the runtime on the affected pool without full deploy? what's the blast radius?

kevin (runtime-lead): yes — small binary flip to route quantized attention to the safe kernel. Two steps: push config flag to runtime agent to skip fast-path, then roll agents. Flag: RUNTIME_QUANT_SAFE=1. rollout target: nodes labeled inference-pool-quant.

maria (oncall-sre): initiated rolling restart of agents on labeled nodes with flag set. command:
```bash
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=quant -o name); do ssh $n 'sudo systemctl restart runtime-agent --env RUNTIME_QUANT_SAFE=1' & done
```

incident-bot: update: 10 nodes restarted, 18 pending.

roch (customer-succ): FYI — we have two enterprise customers complaining about degraded latency and 502s. I'll open a proactive support ticket and offer status.

maria (oncall-sre): after first 10 nodes restarted, west-1 5xx dropped to 1.2%, west-2 steady ~0.8%. overall error budget trending back to normal.

pagerduty: Pager rotation: maria -> jess in 20m for handoff.

jess (eng-oncall): taking over for next phase. kevin, can you push the config flag cluster-wide after we confirm metrics for 10 more minutes?

kevin (runtime-lead): will do. also preparing a hotfix PR to avoid the kvcache race (longer fix) — target merge in 2-3 hours, then a staged canary deploy.

maria (oncall-sre): confirming customer impact summary for postmortem: ~12% 5xx spike at peak, ~8k affected requests in 15m window, two enterprise customers with errors affecting <5% of their calls due to routing to standby. No data exfiltration.

roch (customer-succ): I'll escalate to account teams and share mitigation steps + ETA for permanent fix.

jess (eng-oncall): monitoring is stable. leaving routing changes in place until hotfix merges. final note: we've enabled increased tracing for the kvcache path; expect more detailed stack traces if this reappears.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> partial mitigation in place. follow-up: root cause fix in progress, postmortem + RCA scheduled in 24h.
